Networks can send data along cables or through the air. Wi-Fi uses radio waves and a wireless router so devices can join a network without cables. Bluetooth also uses radio signals, but it links two nearby devices directly, over about 10 metres, after they have been paired. Optical fibre sends data as pulses of light along thin glass strands, giving very high bandwidth over long distances.

Mobile technologies, 4G and 5G, use radio masts to give wireless internet across a wide area, so people can stay connected while they move. To evaluate these technologies, think about five things: speed (bandwidth), range, reliability, security and cost. No single technology is best for everything, so the right choice depends on the situation.

Wi-Fi lets laptops, phones and smart devices connect to a network through a wireless router or access point. It is cheap and quick to set up because no cables are needed, and users can move around a building. However, the signal gets weaker the further you are from the router, and walls and other devices cause interference. Speed also falls when many people share one access point. Older Wi-Fi standards reach about 54 Mbps, while modern standards are much faster.
Got it. Keep going.

A Wi-Fi network should have a strong password and WPA2 or WPA3 encryption. Bluetooth is designed for short distances. It uses very little power and needs no router, which makes it ideal for earbuds, smartwatches, wireless mice and hands-free car kits. Its range is short, it is slower than Wi-Fi and only a few devices can connect at once.
And is there anything people often mix up here?

An optical fibre cable is a bundle of very thin glass strands. Data travels along each strand as pulses of light, and because each strand carries its own signal, a huge amount of data can be sent at the same time. This gives very high bandwidth and speed. Light is not affected by electrical interference, so fibre is reliable near machinery, and it is very hard for a hacker to tap into the cable without being noticed, so data is secure.
Okay. Keep going.

Signals can travel many kilometres with little loss, although repeaters are needed to boost them over very long distances. The main drawback is cost: installing fibre often means digging up roads and paying specialists. The glass can also break if the cable is bent too sharply. Fibre is used for internet backbones, undersea cables and full-fibre broadband to homes.
Go on.

Mobile phone networks divide an area into cells, each served by a mast. Phones send and receive data from the nearest mast using radio waves. 4G gives high-speed data, good enough for streaming HD video and making video calls, and it lowered the cost of mobile data. Because masts are expensive, coverage is best in towns and weaker in rural areas.
Right. Keep going.

Using mobile data also drains the battery faster than Wi-Fi. 5G is faster again and has much lower latency, which means less delay. It can support many more devices in one place, which helps the Internet of Things, cloud gaming and connected vehicles. The highest-speed 5G signals do not travel as far and are blocked by buildings, so many more masts are needed and coverage is still growing.

What about the exam? Where has this come up?

Questions on this lesson often ask you to match technologies to uses or descriptions, as in the 2021 paper, question 11, the 2022 paper, question 8 and the 2023 paper, question 6. Learn one clear feature and one typical use for each technology: Bluetooth for short-range links such as earbuds, Wi-Fi for wireless access to a network in a building, fibre for very fast secure links, 5G for fast, low-latency mobile data. In the 2022 paper, question 8 candidates judged true/false statements about fibre optic, so know the facts exactly: light pulses, glass strands, high bandwidth, not affected by electrical interference, hard to tap, expensive to install. When asked to evaluate or compare, give both an advantage and a disadvantage and use comparative words such as 'faster than' or 'more secure than'. Vague answers like 'it is better' or 'it is quick' earn nothing unless you say what it is compared with.
